title: Hang a forklift fork on the carriage at its removal gap, slide it out and drop its lock pin in the notch that fits the pallet
instruction: Fit the loose fork to the forklift carriage, spaced for the pallet.
context: Forklift operators and mechanics fit a fork by hanging it on the carriage at the removal gap, the one place its bottom hook passes the lower bar, then sliding it out and dropping its lock pin into the notch that matches the pallet's openings; a fork one notch off spears a pallet block (O*NET 53-7051.00 Industrial Truck and Tractor Operators; 49-3042.00 Mobile Heavy Equipment Mechanics). Board tasks extend a handle to its detent, move a shelf pull pin, hang a holder on keyhole studs and drive a pallet jack; none hangs a two-hook part where a gap lets it on, slides it captive and indexes it with its own pin.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left (negative toward the right arm); heights above the table. Table: wood top, arm bases 61 cm apart on its near edge. Carriage (half scale, printed plastic or aluminium, fixed to the table), facing the arms. Top bar: grey, x 33 to 35.4, y -22 to +6, height 8.5 to 10.5. On it a black rib 1 cm tall (top at 11.5): two 3 mm rails along its front and back edges and, between them, five notches (pockets 1.6 cm along y, 1.8 cm along x, 1 cm deep) centred at y -18, -14, -8, -2 and +2; the rib between notches stands 1.5 mm below the rails. Lower bar: a grey front strip x 33 to 34, table to 4 cm, full length; behind and above it a grey keeper strip x 34 to 39.5, height 5.8 to 6.8, full length except the removal gap y -11.5 to -4.5 (7 cm). Back plate: dark grey, x 39.5 to 40.5, y -22.5 to +6.5, 12.5 cm tall, with 0.5 cm end plates joining it to the bars. Two identical forks (yellow printed plastic, 160 g with pin): shank 1.4 (x) x 3 (y) x 11.5 cm tall; tine 8 x 3 x 1.5 cm at the shank's foot, pointing at the arms; top plate 8.7 x 3 x 1 cm on the shank's top, reaching back over the top bar, with a back lip 0.5 cm thick hanging 1.5 cm down behind the bar; bottom hook 2 x 3 x 1.2 cm on the shank's back, 3.3 cm above the fork's foot, with a 0.5 cm lip hanging 1.2 cm down; green grip tab 1.8 (x) x 3 (y) x 3.5 cm tall on the top plate, 0.6 cm from its front end; dark red lock pin 1 x 1 x 3 cm sliding 1.5 cm up and down through the top plate over the rib, with a red knob 1.8 (x) x 3 (y) x 3 cm on top. A hung fork's shank front is at x 31.5, its tine tip at x 23.5 and its foot 1 cm above the table. Reference fork: hung at y +2, pin down in the y +2 notch. New fork: standing on its foot on the table at y -13, shank front at x 28 (tine tip x 20, tab centre x 25.5), pin down. Pallet (blue plastic, fixed): x 15 to 19, y -25 to +9, 6 cm tall: 1 cm decks top and bottom, 4 cm blocks at y -25 to -21, -15 to -1 and +5 to +9, leaving openings 6 cm wide centred at y -18 and y +2.
scoring: At the end, open the grippers, judge with a ruler and a front photo. A fork is hung when its top plate rests on the rib (underside within 3 mm of the rib's top), its back lip is behind the top bar, its bottom hook's lip is behind the front strip and it tilts under 5 degrees. Score 0 unless the reference fork is hung with its pin down in the y +2 notch and the new fork is hung. Then 1.0 if the new fork's pin is down in the y -18 notch (pin within 3 mm of its lowest point, fork centre within 4 mm of y -18: 20 cm from the reference fork's centre), still for 1 s. 0 if its pin is down in the y -14 or y -2 notch: that tine meets a pallet block. Otherwise 0.5 if the fork's centre is 5 cm or more from the gap's centre (y -8), captive under the keeper strip; 0.25 if nearer. A fork on the table, perched, leaning or held above the rib scores 0; pushing cannot hang one.
reset_notes: Lift the new fork's pin, slide the fork back to the gap, lift it off and stand it on its mark on the table (y -13, shank front at x 28). Check the reference fork's pin is down in the y +2 notch.
fidelity: Approximate. The carriage and forks are half-scale rigid boxes; notches are square pockets; the lock pin is a damped vertical slide with end stops, no spring. Fork weight and load capacity are not modelled. The simulator scores the final step without opening the grippers: a fork held with its top plate more than 3 mm above the rib counts as not hung and a pin still held up counts as not down, so a held part never outscores a released one.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (raised both arms toward the carriage, forks left as at the start); demo: 1.0 (right arm hung the loose fork on the carriage, slid it out, released and withdrew)
